result:
Parking the whole roadmap: one of its two committed stages is done, and nothing is left to route. These are the steps, written as tool calls because I have no tools this turn.

**1. Read before writing**
```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # the Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                         # append to it, don't overwrite; create it if absent
Bash: ls specs/completed/                                            # confirm no file there with the same name
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`** under a new section `## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06`. There will be one item for the unticked stage and one for each Ranked-list item. Each item will be self-contained, with `Size:` and `Done when:`, and will follow whatever other fields the schema requires:

- **Closure notices (was Stage 2, Track B).** Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing. It consumes the closure log's live feed. Size: small, one closure-log poll every 10 minutes. Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry. Text-message notices remain out of scope.
- **7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (O2).** This builds on Stage 1's response curve, recorded in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md` (the closure chance rises steeply above 3.1 m, to about 60% at 3.8 m). Size: one model run a day, small, based on Stage 1's 22-minute fit. Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook exists for each lock from the river-level forecast.
- **Per-lock pooled closure curves, all 14 locks (O3).** Size: about 14 times Stage 1's data, which was 1.8 GB over 11 years, so roughly 25 GB. Stage 1 found the four locks with the longest records show close to the same curve, which bears on how much pooling buys. Done when: there is a separate closure curve for each of the 14 locks, pooled across locks.
- **Closure-history map for boat operators (O4).** Size: about a day of work, one static map page. Done when: a closure-history map is published for the canal's boat operators.

**3. Retire the roadmap**
```
Edit specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md   # add under the title: PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete
Bash: git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
```
This roadmap has no synthesized spec, methodology file or critique file to retire with it. The Stage 1 findings file stays in `specs/`, because the O2 and O3 items cite it.

**4. Commit on `main`**
```
Bash: git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Bash: git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete); defer Stage 2 and Track A's ranked items"
```

This parks the closure-notices track (Stage 2) along with Track A, as you asked. If the notices should go ahead under other funding, tell me, and I'll stop Track A only and keep the roadmap live for Stage 2. Otherwise I'll run the steps above as written.
